newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's forestry policy called inconsistent.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's forestry policy called inconsistent.

text.p: Cambodian opposition leader Sam Rainsy on Wednesday dismissed as inconsistent and hasty a new forestry policy aimed at averting a cut-off in donor funds.
"There is no serious will to change the forestry policy because behind the anarchic deforestation is rampant corruption," the Khmer Nation Party (KNP) leader claimed at a media briefing.
The cabinet last week approved a forestry policy pushed by international donors and vowed to end the export of new logs across the Thai-Cambodian border.
The announcement came after mounting donor concern over a perceived absence of government action on logging and methods of accounting for timber revenues.
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) earlier this month threatened to halt payment of $60 million in loans unless the government changed its timber policies by October 31.
"The IMF is right to push the government to take appropriate measures," Sam Rainsy said.
"What they expect from the government now is action...no more nice words, no more unfulfilled promises, no more non-implemented decisions, no more cosmetic measures."
But he added that faced with the October 31 deadline, "The government is panicking and they have just announced hasty and inconsistent measures -- an empty gesture."

The KNP leader claimed the forestry code approved by the cabinet contained serious loopholes and worried that the Agriculture Ministry would do nothing to counter secret contracts with foreign loggers.
He suggested the government was not being serious in the search for an independent auditing firm to help enforce an export control and monitoring system.

Finance Minister Keat Chhon said last week the government was talking to SGS (Societe Generale de Surveillance), a Swiss firm that specialises in pre-shipment inspections but has no experience in the forestry field.
